scope: ROUND-2 adversarial meta-audit of the post-repair unit. Supersedes the round-1 REFUTED audit in this file. Method: (1) claim-by-claim independent reproduction of generator_meta.originality_note, sentence by sentence — every search re-executed here, every 'no bearer found' re-tested, every 'fields unchanged' re-diffed; (2) independent web verification of every named entity in the CURRENT passage; (3) confirmation that the specific round-1 defect is gone; (4) old-name purge grep, key/option-letter diff, entityfix-r2 regate ordering, rationale-quote match. Searches executed 2026-08-04 with Exa web/people search, Exa page fetch, WebFetch against the sv/en Wikipedia and Wikidata APIs, and repo grep. WebSearch was unavailable (session budget exhausted) — engines actually used are named per finding so this audit is itself re-runnable. NOTE: this pass ALSO corrects one of my own round-1 findings (see the Almén note).

findings.stage_challenged: repair/originality_note — near-miss disclosure completeness (entity: Cornelius Rooth)
findings.claim: The note's '[3] NEAR-MISSES FOUND, DISCLOSED RATHER THAN SUPPRESSED' list omits the closest and most domain-relevant surname bearer: Dan-Olof Rooth, a real Swedish ECONOMICS professor. It discloses Mats Rooth (Cornell linguistics, 'unrelated field') and Cornelius Root (American local-newspaper proprietor) while missing the one near-miss that sits in exactly this unit's field.
findings.evidence: Exa web search '"Cornelius Rooth" journalist economics columnist' returned zero exact-name hits (reproducing the note's core claim) but surfaced IDEAS/RePEc author records for Dan-Olof Rooth: 'Lundborg, Petter & Nilsson, Anton & Rooth, Dan-Olof, 2014, "Adolescent health and adult labor market outcomes," Journal of Health Economics 37(C):25-40' (ideas.repec.org/j/J2-9.html); 'Åslund, Olof & Rooth, Dan-Olof, 2007, "Do when and where matter? initial labour market conditions and immigrant earnings," Economic Journal 117(518):422-448'; 'Rooth, Dan-Olof, 2003, IFAU Working Paper Series 2003:7'. A Swedish labour economist publishing in top economics journals is a nearer neighbour to 'Cornelius Rooth, economics columnist' than either disclosed near-miss.
findings.why: NOT refutation-grade and NOT a blocker: the given name differs entirely, no bearer of the full string 'Cornelius Rooth' exists (Exa exact-phrase, sv.wikipedia, en.wikipedia and Wikidata all null), and the campaign's operative standard — the one that triggered the Rundgång rename — is exact-name collision, not shared surname. Round-1's own audit already recorded 'Rooth is a genuine Swedish surname but no journalist, columnist or economist bears the full name', so escalating surname-only now would be inconsistent. The defect is in the note's completeness, not in the item: a section that advertises itself as disclosing what it found should have caught the in-domain bearer before the out-of-domain one. One clause to add; no rename indicated.

findings.stage_challenged: repair/originality_note — [4] source attribution for the removed name
findings.claim: The note quotes rundgangkarlstad.se as STATING 'Rundgång är en kooperativ, cirkulär galleria i Karlstad' and as reporting a March-2025 move to Tingvallagatan 7 plus an offer of 'secondhand, remake, uthyrning, renovering och reparation'. That page yields none of this text to any fetcher I have; the quotation is therefore not reproducible AS ATTRIBUTED, although every factual component of it is independently true from other sources.

Exa page fetch of the same URL → identical result: '# RUNDGÅNG / URL: https://rundgangkarlstad.se/ / RUNDGÅNG'. The site is client-rendered. SUBSTANCE CORROBORATED ELSEWHERE, all reproduced by me: smartakartan.se/karlstad/rundgang/ → 'en cirkulär galleria som samlar framtidens varor och tjänster', address 'Tingvallagatan 7, Karlstad', second-hand / upcycled-remade / resource-smart goods; karlstad.se/smarta-karlstad/innovationsinitiativ/rundgang → 'Alla aktörer hade erbjudanden inom cirkulär ekonomi, till exempel secondhand, remake, reparation eller uthyrning'; karlstad.se/.../klimatneutrala-karlstad-2030/rundgang → 'Rundgång – en cirkulär popup-galleria som blev permanent … drivs konceptet vidare i kooperativ regi'; karlstad.mynewsdesk.com press release 2024-01-02 'Karlstads cirkulära galleria blir permanent – i kooperativ regi'; vf.se 2025-01-04 'Popup-gallerian Rundgång flyttar till Tingvallagatan i Karlstad' and vf.se 2025-03-27 'Nu har gallerian flyttat – Rundgång öppnar på Tingvallagatan' (the March-2025 move); viablecities.se/kunskap/cirkular-galleria/ → 'second hand, remake, uthyrning och lagning'.
findings.why: The repair's CORE JUSTIFICATION reproduces in full and independently: the removed name belonged to a real Swedish second-hand-and-repair circular retail operator, i.e. exactly this unit's domain. So the rename premise is sound and there is no bar to ship. The wart is citation hygiene in a note that bills itself as 'a LOG OF SEARCHES ACTUALLY EXECUTED … so any auditor can re-run it': the one direct quotation attributed to a primary source is the one an auditor cannot re-run. Re-attribute to karlstad.se / smartakartan.se / vf.se and the entry becomes fully reproducible. Likewise not reproducible by me in the same entry: the parenthetical 'Järnvägsgatan 14' address for the Mitt i City popup — the kommun pages I fetched name 'Mitt i City' without that street number.

findings.stage_challenged: the round-1 refutation defect — verified cured
findings.claim: The exact assertion this unit was REFUTED for is gone from the shipped artifact, and its correction is independently true.
findings.evidence: Round-1 refutation was: originality_note asserted 'a second real bearer is a long-running Gothenburg second-hand record shop'. In the current file that string survives only inside the note's own recital of what round 1 said, immediately followed by 'This note replaces that text', and by an explicit correction: 'the record shop Rundgång is in MALMÖ, not Gothenburg (Kristianstadsgatan 14 …)' and '"A long-running Gothenburg second-hand record shop" is WITHDRAWN as inaccurate.' I verified the correction independently — six sources place the shop at Kristianstadsgatan 14, Möllevången, Malmö, trading since 2004 in new and second-hand vinyl — and no Gothenburg record shop of that name surfaced in any search. The round-1 audit's competing detail (that the Gothenburg bearer is 'Studio Rundgång', a studio rather than a shop) is not contradicted by the new note, which now makes no Gothenburg claim at all.
findings.why: Defect genuinely removed, not merely reworded, and removed in the direction of demonstrable truth. The retained recital is required for the audit trail to be legible and is clearly marked as superseded.

findings.stage_challenged: verdicts-vfinal regate ordering (entityfix-r2 lines are LAST where they exist)
findings.claim: Fresh entityfix-r2 lines exist and are the LAST records for this unit in four of five vfinal files; the fifth carries no entityfix line of either generation, matching the batch-4 convention this audit recorded in round 1.
findings.evidence: verdicts-gdistractor.jsonl (25 lines): this unit's records at 6-10 (G-DISTRACTOR), 16-20 (G-DISTRACTOR-entityfix), 21-25 (G-DISTRACTOR-entityfix-r2) — r2 last. verdicts-gkey-1.jsonl (25): 6-10, 16-20 (entityfix, bare 'q1'..'q5'), 21-25 (entityfix-r2, bare 'q1'..'q5') — r2 last. verdicts-gkey-2.jsonl (25): 6-10, 16-20, 21-25 (entityfix-r2) — r2 last. verdicts-gstem.jsonl (10, unit-exclusive): 1-5 entityfix, 6-10 entityfix-r2, all pass — r2 last. verdicts-gkey-resolved.jsonl (30): this unit's last records are 21-25, pre-repair G-KEY vote-2 records; zero entityfix and zero entityfix-r2 lines. All 15 r2 records carry executed_by 'claude-opus-4-8/G-<GATE>-entityfix-r2'. G-KEY r2 re-solve = pass on all five gaps in both voters, consistent with keys C/A/D/B/C.
findings.why: Ordering invariant satisfied wherever entityfix runs at all. The gkey-resolved gap is the pre-existing batch-4 convention (batches 1, 2, 3, 5 and 12 likewise carry zero; only batch 14 propagates), and is semantically harmless because the resolved votes already equal the r2 re-solve.

findings.claim: The r2 distractor regate did not reproduce the entityfix pass's q:5 'seams' flag and raised a new q:4 'mercantile' flag instead. Both are self-described as beatable; neither is a kill.
findings.evidence: entityfix (line 20, q:5, flag, severity major, quote 'seams'): 'ARGUABLE … Beatable: the fixed idiom is "slip through the cracks" … Pre-existing and rename-independent'. entityfix-r2 (line 24, q:4, flag, severity major, quote 'mercantile'): 'ARGUABLE … beaten by the evidence sentence the writer puts immediately after the gap … Key support remains clearly stronger than the distractor case'; r2 records q:5 as pass with empty findings. I judged both defences sound against the passage text: 'slip through the cracks' is the fixed idiom and the sentence carries no garment metaphor; and 'more mercantile than the applause admits' is defeated by the immediately following insolvency sentence, which underwrites precariousness rather than commercialism, so 'fragile' remains the only reading satisfying both the polarity frame and the downstream evidence.
findings.why: Flag-vs-flag non-determinism across regate generations on genuinely arguable distractors, with 0 kills in both passes. Recorded for visibility, not as a defect: the item survives either flag on the merits.
